The ISS will pass within 412 m of the COSMOS 1408 debris in 18 hours, with a collision probability of 0.00031 (1 in 3226). This means there is roughly one chance in three thousand two hundred twenty-six that the two objects could collide at their closest approach, which is the point of minimum separation. A maneuver is recommended: fire the thrusters 6 hours before the encounter, adding 0.42 m/s prograde to increase the miss distance to about 4.2 km and reduce the collision probability to 2.3 × 10⁻⁸. No other events are expected. A human operator must approve any maneuver.
